name: Galloway Run-Walk-Run

citations.title: Run-Walk-Run method and Magic Mile time trial

description: The Run-Walk-Run method: every workout — including races — uses planned run/walk intervals (e.g., 30 sec run / 30 sec walk, or 4 min run / 30 sec walk). Anchored to the Magic Mile time trial. Famous for accessibility, injury resistance, and enabling first-time and masters runners to complete marathons.
signature: Run-Walk-Run intervals throughout every run; Magic Mile time trial as the fitness anchor
philosophyNarrative: Galloway's revolutionary insight: walking breaks during continuous running don't slow you down — they speed you up. Inserting planned walk breaks (the 'Run-Walk-Run' or RWR method) keeps muscles fresher, prevents the cumulative fatigue that wrecks pacing, and makes recovery between hard efforts almost instant. The system is anchored on a 'Magic Mile' time trial — a single, all-out mile run periodically — which derives all other paces. Run-walk ratios scale with experience: beginners might run 30 seconds and walk 30 seconds; advanced runners might run 4 minutes and walk 30 seconds. The RWR pattern is used in EVERY run including races. The result: dramatically lower injury rates, accessibility for runners who can't run continuously for hours, and surprising results — many Galloway runners post personal bests using walk breaks. Especially powerful for first-time marathoners, masters athletes, and anyone returning from injury.

paceZones.purpose: Most weekly running. Galloway prescribes long-run pace = magic mile + 2 min/mile slower as a starting point. RWR ratio applied throughout.

rpeRange.description: Comfortable; RWR breaks make this very sustainable

paceZones.purpose: User's goal race pace. Galloway's published formulas: 5K = MM + 0:33/mi; 10K = MM + 1:00/mi; HM = MM + 1:20/mi; Marathon = MM + 3:00/mi.

rpeRange.description: Race effort, varies by distance — RWR makes this sustainable

paceZones.purpose: Time-trial pace. Run every 3-4 weeks to recalibrate fitness. Equivalent to all-out 1-mile race pace.

workouts.name: Easy Run with Run-Walk-Run
workouts.shortDescription: Easy aerobic run using assigned RWR ratio (30:30, 1:1, 2:1, etc.)

mainSet.cue: Apply your RWR ratio (e.g., 30:30 or 1:1) throughout. Walk breaks brisk — walking, not strolling.

workouts.purpose: Aerobic base building with built-in recovery. RWR keeps stress on muscles and joints low while still building cardiovascular fitness.
cues: Walk breaks should be brisk (~3.5 mph), not strolling
Use a run-walk timer or app to maintain ratio
If pace feels too easy, that's correct — RWR is intentionally moderate

workouts.name: Long Run with Run-Walk-Run
workouts.shortDescription: Long run using RWR ratio, often EXCEEDING race distance for marathon

mainSet.description: Long run with run-walk intervals throughout
mainSet.cue: Galloway long runs often exceed race distance (up to 26-29 mi for marathon!) because RWR keeps fatigue low. Pace is intentionally slow.

workouts.purpose: Endurance building. Galloway's marathon plans famously include 26-29 mile long runs (above race distance) — possible only because RWR keeps fatigue low. Builds extreme race-day confidence.
cues: Pace 2-3 minutes per mile slower than goal race pace
Use shorter run intervals than your normal RWR if pace creeps up
Practice race-day fueling on runs over 90 min

workouts.name: Magic Mile Time Trial
workouts.shortDescription: All-out 1-mile time trial used every 3-4 weeks to recalibrate fitness

mainSet.cue: Controlled-fast first quarter, settle into rhythm, push the last quarter. Time accurately — this number drives all paces.

workouts.purpose: Fitness anchor. Galloway's Magic Mile predicts race times across all distances via published formulas. Run every 3-4 weeks to track progress and recalibrate paces.
cues: Use the result to update training paces

workouts.name: Race Pace Run with RWR
workouts.shortDescription: Run at goal race pace using race-day RWR ratio

mainSet.description: Continuous run at race pace using race-day RWR ratio
mainSet.cue: Use the exact RWR ratio you'll race with. This rehearses race-day rhythm.

workouts.purpose: Race-day rehearsal. Practices the RWR rhythm you'll use in the race so it's automatic on race day.
cues: Use your race-day RWR ratio exactly
Goal pace from the start — no easing in
Practice taking water/fuel during walk breaks

workouts.name: Cadence Drills
workouts.shortDescription: Optional turnover work — short fast intervals for cadence development

mainSet.cue: Quick turnover, short stride. Count steps for 30 sec — aim for 90+ per leg.

workouts.purpose: Improves cadence and running economy. Optional in Galloway plans; especially useful for masters runners and those working on form.
cues: Short, quick steps — not long strides

workouts.name: Cross-Training
workouts.shortDescription: Optional aerobic supplement on non-running days

mainSet.cue: Easy aerobic effort. Cycling or pool running preferred.

workouts.purpose: Aerobic supplement without running impact. Galloway encourages cross-training for aerobic capacity, especially for masters runners.

phases.name: Base
phases.focus: Establish RWR pattern, build short-run consistency, first Magic Mile.
phases.athleteNarrative: Welcome to Galloway. The first thing to learn is the Run-Walk-Run rhythm. Use a run-walk timer or app — every workout uses your assigned ratio. Beginners typically start with 30 seconds run / 30 seconds walk; we'll adjust as your fitness grows. The first Magic Mile time trial happens at the end of week 3 or 4 to set your training paces. Don't worry if it feels slow — RWR is supposed to feel sustainable.

phases.name: Build
phases.focus: Long runs extend; second/third Magic Mile recalibrates pace; race-pace runs introduced.
phases.athleteNarrative: Build phase. Long runs extend dramatically — Galloway plans famously go beyond race distance. The Magic Mile is run every 3-4 weeks to track fitness gains and update your paces. A weekly race-pace run begins, using your exact race-day RWR ratio. Trust the long runs — they feel slow but they're banking endurance you'll cash in on race day.

phases.name: Peak
phases.focus: Peak long run (often longer than race distance), final pace runs, race confidence.
phases.athleteNarrative: Peak phase. For marathon plans, this is where you do a 26-mile long run — the unique Galloway approach of going AT or above race distance. RWR makes this possible without depleting you. Final Magic Mile sets race expectations. Race-pace runs lock in your race-day rhythm. You're ready.

phases.name: Taper
phases.focus: Reduce volume; preserve RWR rhythm; arrive fresh.
phases.athleteNarrative: Taper. Volume drops, but the RWR rhythm continues so race day feels familiar. A short pace run mid-week confirms your race-day pace. Sleep, hydrate, trust the work.

weeklyPatterns.notes: Galloway 3-day pattern. Most accessible — 2 easy runs midweek + Sunday long run. Excellent for first-time marathoners and masters athletes.

schedule.notes: Race pace OR Magic Mile (every 3-4 wk)

weeklyPatterns.notes: Build phase 3-day. Thursday alternates between race-pace run and Magic Mile.
4-day build pattern. Adds a third weekly run with optional cadence drills.
Recovery week — every 3 weeks. Volume reduced, no quality session.

raceWeekSchedule.notes: 2 mi at race pace with RWR
RACE DAY — use your trained RWR ratio

taper.notes: Galloway taper is gentle — RWR makes the system inherently low-fatigue, so dramatic taper isn't needed. 2 weeks at 65%/40% volume.

strengthRecommendation.philosophy: Galloway emphasizes core stability and form drills over heavy lifting. If user opts in via onboarding, recommend a short core/glute routine (10-15 min) on rest days. Avoid heavy strength work — Galloway runners often have masters runner profiles where excessive load isn't beneficial.

crossTrainingRecommendation.intensityGuidance: Galloway plans explicitly include cross-training as a rest-day option. Easy aerobic effort, 30-60 min. Especially valuable for masters runners and runners managing minor injuries.

restrictions.rule: Elite runners targeting fast times generally don't use RWR — though many advanced runners benefit from it for ultras and recovery from injury.
restrictions.warningMessage: Galloway is excellent for accessibility, recovery, and ultras — but if you're targeting an elite-level time, a continuous-running method (Daniels, Pfitzinger) may be more pace-specific.

restrictions.rule: Run-walk-run requires the user to be willing to take walk breaks during races and training. Some runners psychologically resist this.
restrictions.warningMessage: Galloway requires walk breaks during EVERY run, including races. If the idea of walking during a race feels wrong, this method may not work for you — but consider that many Galloway runners post personal bests using it.

invariants: RWR ratio applied to EVERY run, including races
Magic Mile time trial every 3-4 weeks for fitness recalibration
Long run can EXCEED race distance for marathon (up to 26-29 mi) — RWR makes this safe
Long run cap at 55% of weekly mileage (much higher than other methods due to RWR)
Cutback every 3 weeks at 65% — Galloway uses more frequent recovery weeks
Beginners: 3 days/week is the standard; do not push higher
Walk breaks must be brisk (~3.5 mph), not strolling
If user resists walk breaks, suggest Higdon Novice as alternative
